title: Keyword-priority cause selection masking the real metric
objective: Confirm the mock's fixed keyword priority (tension > calibration > roller > yarn) doesn't override the actually-queried metric when a retrieved incident mentions an unrelated keyword.
input_scenario: Query about 'strength', but the one retrieved incident's 'reason' happens to mention 'tension' in an unrelated clause.
expected_behavior: Cause determination should weigh relevance/similarity, not just string-match the first keyword found.

recommendations.expected_outcome: Stabilize tension settings and reduce variability

diagnosis.additional_notes: Analysis based on 5 anomalies detected in strength for inconsistent symptoms on loom 12, batch B102.

severity_justification_hint: Misattributed cause due to naive keyword matching can misdirect maintenance effort.
observations: Although the queried metric was strength and the retrieved incident had only 0.3 similarity, the system selected “Tension setting misalignment” as the primary cause based on the unrelated tension keyword.
conclusion: The cause selection was influenced by fixed keyword priority rather than evidence relevance, resulting in a potentially misattributed root cause.
